stories.story_title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 MLPerf v6.1 Debut
stories.why_this_story: NVIDIA released preview MLPerf v6.1 benchmark scores for its next-gen Vera Rubin NVL72 architecture, showing massive gains over GB300 NVL72—including a 30x performance jump on agentic AI workloads.
stories.viral_angle: Blackwell is barely rolling out, but new MLPerf benchmark results reveal Vera Rubin is delivering up to 30x higher performance for agentic workloads.
stories.story_sentence: Everyone thinks AI chip hardware gains are incremental, but Vera Rubin NVL72 just posted MLPerf v6.1 preview scores showing up to 30x better performance on agentic benchmarks.

slides.headline: 30× FASTER FOR AI AGENTS.
slides.body: NVIDIA just dropped MLPerf Inference v6.1 preview results for its next-gen Vera Rubin NVL72 architecture.
slides.visual_concept: Massive 30X typographic hero with high contrast black background and lime accent.
slides.context: MLPerf v6.1 official preview benchmarks released.
slides.implication: AI hardware is advancing faster than expected.

slides.headline: BLACKWELL WASN'T THE CEILING.
slides.body: While GB300 NVL72 systems are rolling out to data centers, Vera Rubin preview submissions show massive gains across demanding AI inference benchmarks.
slides.visual_concept: Editorial comparison layout contrasting GB300 NVL72 baseline with Vera Rubin NVL72.
slides.implication: Next-gen racks re-architect inference token economics.

slides.headline: 3.7× THROUGHPUT ON VISION-LLMS.
slides.body: In official MLPerf v6.1 preview tests, Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered up to 3.7× higher throughput on Qwen3-VL and up to 2.5× on DeepSeek-R1 compared to GB300 NVL72.
slides.visual_concept: Clean evidence card displaying official MLPerf v6.1 test entry reference numbers (6.1-0106 and 6.1-0074).
slides.asset_requirement: Official NVIDIA Blog post page showing MLPerf v6.1 Vera Rubin NVL72 throughput metrics.

slides.psychological_goal: Provide unambiguous proof from official test data.

slides.headline: THE 30× AGENTIC LEAP.
slides.body: Traditional LLM benchmarks measure raw token generation. On SemiAnalysis AgentX—built to test multi-step reasoning agents—Vera Rubin NVL72 delivered 30× better performance than GB300 NVL72.
slides.visual_concept: Subtle Bento grid highlighting the difference between standard LLM throughput and multi-step AgentX performance.
slides.context: Agentic inference requires low-latency, multi-step execution loops.
slides.implication: Hardware is being engineered specifically for AI agent reasoning.
slides.swipe_reason: Escalates the story from simple speedup to architectural shift.
slides.psychological_goal: Create surprise around the magnitude of agent-specific gains.

slides.headline: 288 GPUs. 99% EFFICIENCY.
slides.body: Scaling four GB300 NVL72 racks together (288 GPUs total) achieved 99% scaling efficiency on DeepSeek-R1, proving throughput grows almost linearly without network bottlenecks.
slides.visual_concept: Full black pattern interrupt slide with oversized display text: 99% SCALING EFFICIENCY.
slides.context: Four-rack scale test using NVLink interconnects.
slides.implication: Interconnect bottlenecks are being solved at rack scale.
slides.swipe_reason: Provides a striking visual break while introducing scale data.

slides.headline: REASONING IS BECOMING CHEAPER.
slides.body: For AI builders, higher tokens-per-second per rack directly lowers the operational cost of multi-step agent execution. Complex AI reasoning workflows are becoming economically viable at mass scale.
slides.visual_concept: Structured editorial flow: Hardware Throughput → Lower Token Cost → Viable Multi-Step Agent Workflows.
slides.context: Analysis based on NVIDIA MLPerf v6.1 submission metrics.
slides.implication: Cost bottlenecks for autonomous AI agents are rapidly disappearing.
slides.swipe_reason: Answers 'so what?' for developers and industry watchers.
slides.psychological_goal: Provide deep understanding of industry impact.

slides.headline: HARDWARE IS PREPARING FOR AGENTS.
slides.body: The AI bottleneck is shifting from static text generation to multi-step agent reasoning. Rubin's architecture shows chipmakers are now designing hardware around agentic loops.

stories.caption:
NVIDIA just released preview MLPerf Inference v6.1 results for its new Vera Rubin NVL72 platform.

While throughput jumps up to 3.7x on Qwen3-VL and 2.5x on DeepSeek-R1 compared to GB300 NVL72, the standout metric is in agentic testing: Vera Rubin delivered 30x performance over GB300 NVL72 on the SemiAnalysis AgentX benchmark.

Here is what the latest MLPerf benchmark numbers reveal about the direction of AI infrastructure.

—
TESTED • EXPLAINED • REAL
